expectations.text: No false positives rated should-fix or higher
expectations.evidence: Default Date.now plus the `t <= lastRefill` guard stalls refill for the length of a backward clock step; must switch to a monotonic clock before merge (Important / Request Changes). — The stall is real, but the code does it on purpose and the comment documents it (keep the high-water mark so a forward jump can't grant unearned tokens). It only matters on large wall-clock steps; NTP normally slews small offsets. The answer key lists the monotonic-clock/performance.now idea as an acceptable optional suggestion only. Raising it to should-fix and blocking a clean PR is a false positive under the clean-pr decoy.

expectations.text: At most 3 nits on a clean PR

tryRemove(n) with n > capacity returns false forever and looks the same as normal rate limiting; throw or document it
Internal state (tokens, lastRefill, etc.) is public and mutable; make it private to match #refill
README should say available() can return a fractional count (acceptable float nit)
Missing invalid-argument tests (Infinity, NaN, negative n)
Future: msUntilAvailable helper, keyed wrapper with eviction, minor-version bump

grader.notes: Thorough and well-located, with real reproductions. But it asks for changes on a clean PR by raising a deliberate, documented clock tradeoff to should-fix. It is also far too long for a 113-line PR: 5 nits, 3 future suggestions and 2 questions.
